title: The Road to the Conquest
subtitle: The Rupture of the Hudaybiyyah Pact, the Midnight Raid at Al-Watir, and the Cry of Khuza'ah
summary: Under the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah, Arab tribes were guaranteed the right to enter formal alliances with either Quraysh or the Muslims. When Banu Bakr, actively aided by prominent Quraysh chieftains, launched a treacherous nocturnal assault against Banu Khuza'ah at the spring of Al-Watir within the sacred territory, the ten-year truce was shattered. Amr ibn Salim al-Khuza'i rode urgently to Madinah to seek prophetic justice, setting in motion the inevitable march toward Makkah.

sections.text: Signed in the sixth year of the Hijrah, the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah had established a ten-year non-aggression pact between the nascent Islamic state and the oligarchy of Quraysh. A crucial clause in the agreement stipulated that any Arab tribe wishing to enter into a mutual covenant with Muhammad ﷺ was free to do so, and any tribe wishing to enter into an alliance with Quraysh was equally free. Under this clause, the venerable tribe of Banu Khuza'ah formally aligned itself with the Muslims, while their longstanding rivals, Banu Bakr, joined the alliance of Quraysh.

For nearly two years, the peace held, facilitating trade and unprecedented inter-tribal dialogue. However, deep-seated pre-Islamic blood feuds still simmered beneath the surface. Banu Bakr harbored an ancient thirst for revenge stemming from a homicide that predated the treaty, and their chieftain, Nawfal ibn Mu'awiyah al-Dili, sought an opportune moment to strike at Khuza'ah.
The Treacherous Nocturnal Ambush at Al-Watir

In Sha'ban of the eighth year of the Hijrah, Nawfal led a nocturnal war party against an unsuspecting encampment of Khuza'ah gathered around the spring of Al-Watir in Lower Makkah. The assault was carried out with the covert complicity of several influential leaders of Quraysh—including Safwan ibn Umayyah, Ikrima ibn Abi Jahl, and Suhayl ibn Amr—who provided weapons, warhorses, and participated in disguise under the cover of darkness.

Caught completely unprepared, the men of Khuza'ah fled into the sacred precinct of the Kaaba, believing that ancient sanctity would protect them from slaughter. When Nawfal's fighters pursued them into the Haram, some cautioned: 'O Nawfal, we have entered the sanctuary! Beware of your God!' But Nawfal disregarded the sacred boundary, answering: 'There is no God today, O Banu Bakr! Take your revenge!' Over twenty innocent members of Khuza'ah were killed in cold blood within the sacred sanctuary.
The Cry of Amr ibn Salim in the Prophet's Mosque

Following the massacre, forty horsemen of Khuza'ah rode frantically across the desert toward Madinah to inform the Prophet of the brazen violation of the treaty. Entering the Prophet's Mosque while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sat among the companions, their leader, Amr ibn Salim al-Khuza'i, stood before him and recited stirring verses recounting their ancient alliance and the atrocity at Al-Watir:

يَا رَبِّ إِنِّي نَاشِدٌ مُحَمَّدَا * حِلْفَ أَبِينَا وَأَبِيهِ الأَتْلَدَا
هُمْ بَيَّتُونَا بِالْوَتِيرِ هُجَّدَا * وَقَتَلُونَا رُكَّعًا وَسُجَّدَا
'O Lord! I appeal to Muhammad by the ancient covenant between our forebears and his! They attacked us at Al-Watir while we were asleep, and slaughtered us while we were bowing and prostrating!' (Al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah by Ibn Hisham)

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ rose to his feet with solemn determination and proclaimed: 'You shall be aided, O Amr ibn Salim!' Looking toward a rising cloud on the horizon, the Prophet remarked: 'Indeed, this cloud heralds the aid of Banu Ka'b.'
The Failed Mission of Abu Sufyan

Realizing the catastrophic strategic error they had committed, the chiefs of Quraysh sent their paramount leader, Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, to Madinah in a desperate bid to mend the rift, disclaim responsibility, and renew the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah. Abu Sufyan entered Madinah filled with deep apprehension.

Abu Sufyan approached the Prophet, but the Messenger of Allah ﷺ met his overtures with absolute silence. Desperate for intercession, Abu Sufyan sought out Abu Bakr, then Umar, and finally Ali ibn Abi Talib and Fatimah, pleading for someone to advocate for Quraysh. Umar answered with fierce rebuff: 'Shall I intercede for you with the Messenger of Allah? By Allah, if I found nothing but small ants, I would wage war against you with them!' Having exhausted all avenues and realizing that the decree of justice was sealed, Abu Sufyan returned to Makkah empty-handed, leaving Quraysh paralyzed with anxiety.

The betrayal at Al-Watir transformed the political trajectory of Arabia. The breach of the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah removed the legal impediment to liberating Makkah from polytheism. The road was now irrevocably cleared for the greatest and most consequential expedition in early Islamic history: the peaceful Conquest of Makkah.
